cards.front: One complication of severe, prolonged vitamin [ B 1 (thiamine) ] deficiency is [ Wernicke-Korsakoff ] syndrome
cards.raw0: One complication of severe, prolonged vitamin {{c2::B1 (thiamine)}} deficiency is {{c1::Wernicke-Korsakoff}} syndrome
cards.back: - Often in patients with chronic alcohol use disorder with suspected malnutrition ; the two occur together and have the same etiology but are two distinct conditions ↓ Thiamine leads to ↓ ATP and ↑ ROS synthesis, leading to neuronal injury - Wernicke encephalopathy is reversible and presents with classic triad of confusion , ataxia , and nystagmus/ophthalmoplegia - Korsakoff syndrome is a later complication of prolonged B 1 deficiency that is irreversible and presents with a triad of confabulations (buzzword), anterograde/retrograde amnesia , and personality changes - Korsakoff syndrome represents damage to the limbic system, especially the mammillary bodies of the hypothalamus [img] [img]

cards.front: Adrenoleukodystrophy is due to a mutation in a(n) [peroxisomal] membrane transporter, preventing very long chain fatty acids (VLCFAs) from being tagged with [ coenzyme A ]

cards.front: In which order should thiamine and glucose be given in the treatment of alcohol withdrawal ? [Thiamine then glucose]
cards.raw0:
In which order should thiamine and glucose be given in the treatment of alcohol withdrawal?

{{c1::Thiamine then glucose}}
cards.back: Thiamine allows proper processing of glucose through metabolic pathway A: in CAC T: from PPP to glycolysis P: pyruvate to acetyl-CoA (glycolysis to TCA) "ATP" because deficiency of B1 leads to low ATP (no CAC) - therefore when giving glucose without thiamine you're adding "fuel to the fire" ATP on a branch

cards.front: Ketoacidosis and hypoglycemia may indicate [alcoholic ketoacidosis]
cards.raw0: Ketoacidosis and hypoglycemia may indicate {{c1::alcoholic ketoacidosis::condition}}
cards.back: Glucose ≤ 250 Hypoglycemia : ↑ NADH = ↓ oxaloacetate (shuttled to malate) ↓ oxaloacetate for GNG ↑ NADH = ↓ lactate to pyruvate ↓ pyruvate for GNG Ketoacidosis : ↓ oxaloacetate = acetyl-CoA cannot combine with oxaloacetate to enter TCA and instead shuttled to ketones

cards.front: What is the likely diagnosis in a pregnant patient that develops encephalopathy , nystagmus , and gait ataxia after several days of hyperemesis gravidarum ? [Wernicke encephalopathy]
cards.raw0:
What is the likely diagnosis in a pregnant patient that develops encephalopathy, nystagmus, and gait ataxia after several days of hyperemesis gravidarum?

{{c1::Wernicke encephalopathy}}
cards.back: - Secondary to thiamine deficiency - This triad is only present in ∼30% of patients with Wernicke encephalopathy per AMBOSS - Seen in alcohol use disorder (most common) or other severely malnourished patients (e.g., anorexia nervosa, hyperemesis gravidarum) - Korsakoff syndrome symptoms include confabulation , personality change , and permanent memory loss [img] [img]

cards.front: What is the treatment regimen for diabetic ketoacidosis ? - IV [fluids], IV [insulin], and [potassium (if ≤ 5.2)] - Once the anion gap closes : [subQ insulin] - Once blood glucose reaches 200 - 250 mg/dL: [D5W]
cards.raw0:
What is the treatment regimen for diabetic ketoacidosis?

- IV {{c1::fluids}}, IV {{c1::insulin}}, and {{c1::potassium (if ≤ 5.2)}}
- Once the anion gap closes: {{c2::subQ insulin}}
- Once blood glucose reaches 200 - 250 mg/dL: {{c3::D5W}}
cards.back: - Insulin infusion should be continued for 1 - 2 hrs after subcutaneous administration for bridging - D5W is to prevent hypoglycemia; monitor K + , Mg 2+ , and PO 4 3- - Admit patients to the ICU (insulin drip)

cards.front: [ Adrenoleukodystrophy ] is the accumulation of very-long-chain fatty acids in the adrenals, testes, and white matter , presenting as cognitive, visual, hearing, and motor dysfunction
cards.raw0: {{c1::Adrenoleukodystrophy}} is the accumulation of very-long-chain fatty acids in the adrenals, testes, and white matter, presenting as cognitive, visual, hearing, and motor dysfunction
cards.back: - Inheritance: X-linked, males affected - Pathophysiology: mutation in ABCD1 gene → defective production of adrenoleukodystrophy protein ( ALDP ) in the membrane of peroxisomes → decreased metabolism of very long chain fatty acids ( VLCFA ) → accumulation of VLCFAs toxic to adrenal glands, myelin (significant accumulation in CNS, adrenals, testes ) - Symptoms: developmental/behavioral problems, vision problems, poor coordination, adrenal insufficiency, difficulty swallowing, paraparesis
